comparison_block.heading: Libertex vs eToro — Which Is Better in 2026?
comparison_block.body: Both offer real stock investing alongside CFDs, both are CySEC regulated, and both bet on proprietary platforms over MetaTrader-only approaches. Libertex wins on pricing transparency — zero spreads with a known commission means you always know your cost before clicking. eToro wins on social trading (CopyTrader is unmatched), instrument count (7,300+ vs 600+), and geographic reach (six licences vs one). For the cost-conscious European trader who values predictability over community, Libertex. For the social investor who wants copy trading, broader asset coverage, and multi-regulation — eToro takes it despite higher forex costs.

sections.heading: Is Libertex Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
A broker group that has survived nearly 30 years in the markets since 1997 is not an overnight operation making promises. The Libertex Group — operating through Indication Investments Ltd under CySEC licence 164/12 — has built its identity around one genuinely distinctive proposition: zero spreads, commission only. Every trade you enter, the cost is transparent before you click. No widening at news time. No variable markup hidden in the spread. Just a flat percentage commission starting at 0.006% for forex.

That sounds revolutionary until you do the maths. On a standard EUR/USD lot ($100,000 notional), 0.006% per side equals $6 per side — $12 round-turn. Raw-spread ECN brokers like Pepperstone or IC Markets charge $7 round-turn commission plus a spread of 0.0-0.2 pips. All-in, those ECN brokers cost $7-9 per lot. Libertex costs $12. You are paying a transparency premium of $3-5 per lot for the certainty of knowing your exact cost before entering.

For some traders, that premium is worth it. If you despise variable spreads that widen during news releases and cannot stomach uncertainty in your cost structure, Libertex delivers something competitors genuinely do not — absolute predictability. The question is whether predictability at a premium is more valuable to you than cheaper execution with slight variability. NAFT rates Libertex 7.0/10 in May 2026.

sections.heading: Is Libertex Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Single-jurisdiction regulation: CySEC, Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission. Indication Investments Ltd holds CIF licence 164/12, granted in 2012. This provides EU/EEA passporting — meaning Libertex can legally serve clients across all European Economic Area member states without separate licences in each country. ICF (Investor Compensation Fund) protection covers up to EUR 20,000 per client if the firm becomes insolvent.

The Libertex Group itself dates to 1997 — making it one of the longest-operating retail trading brands in existence. That longevity provides a degree of track-record trust that newer CySEC brokers cannot claim. However, the absence of FCA (UK), ASIC (Australia), or any other Tier-1 regulator means clients outside the EU must rely solely on CySEC oversight.

NSSMC Ukraine added Libertex to its warning list for operating without a local Ukrainian licence. This is a regional regulatory note — Ukraine requires separate authorisation that Libertex has not obtained. It is not equivalent to a global fraud warning and does not trigger NAFT's kill-switch protocol. But it indicates the firm accepted clients from Ukraine without the required local permit — a compliance gap worth noting.

LBX is a newer entity (established 2024) under the Libertex Group offering MT4/MT5 access. It operates under the same CySEC umbrella. NAFT last reviewed Libertex regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: Libertex Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
The defining feature: zero spreads on all instruments. No variable spread, no markup, no widening. Instead, you pay a flat commission expressed as a percentage of the notional trade value. For forex (EUR/USD), the minimum commission is 0.006% per side — translating to $6 per side or $12 round-turn on a standard lot of $100,000.

Compare this to the ECN benchmark: Pepperstone Razor charges $3.50 per side ($7 RT) plus a raw spread averaging 0.09 pips (approximately $0.90). Total all-in cost: approximately $7.90 per lot. Libertex at $12 is 52% more expensive on a pure cost basis. The premium you pay is for certainty — Libertex's cost never varies, while ECN spreads can widen to 2-5 pips during high-impact news.

On the proprietary Libertex platform, commissions can reach up to 0.3% for certain instruments — particularly stocks and crypto CFDs. That means a $10,000 stock CFD position might cost $30 per side ($60 round-turn). Check the specific commission for your preferred instruments before committing.

The Invest Account offers genuine stock ownership — not CFD wrappers — with zero commission. 300+ real stocks available for buy-and-hold investors. This is Libertex's most competitive offering: commission-free stock investing under CySEC regulation with genuine share ownership and dividends.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of Libertex?
sections.body:
Deposits are instant via card (Visa/Mastercard), Skrill, Neteller, and crypto. Bank wire takes 3-5 business days. Minimum deposit is $100 across all methods. No deposit fees charged by Libertex — though your bank or payment provider may apply their own charges.

Withdrawals process within 1-5 business days depending on method. E-wallets (Skrill, Neteller) are fastest at 1-2 days. Card withdrawals take 3-5 days due to banking processing. Bank wire can take up to 5 business days. Libertex does not charge withdrawal fees on standard requests — a positive contrast to brokers like eToro that charge $5 per withdrawal.

Minimum trade size on the proprietary Libertex platform is EUR 20. This is relevant for position sizing — you cannot open micro-positions below this threshold on the Libertex platform. MT4/MT5 accounts via LBX offer standard lot sizing with micro-lot (0.01) support.

sections.heading: Libertex Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Community feedback across aggregator sites shows generally positive withdrawal experiences for verified accounts. The 55Brokers rating of 4.0-4.5 out of 5 across categories suggests above-average client satisfaction. No systemic withdrawal complaint patterns are visible in public forums at the volume that would trigger concern.

The positive pattern: once KYC is complete and the account is fully verified, withdrawals process within stated timeframes. E-wallet users consistently report 1-2 day turnarounds. The zero-fee structure means you receive exactly what you request — no deductions on Libertex's side.

The caution: Libertex is smaller than giants like eToro or Plus500. Fewer public reviews means less statistical confidence. If a withdrawal stalls, the CySEC complaint mechanism is your recourse — file with CySEC directly if unresolved within 10 business days. ICF EUR 20,000 covers insolvency but not operational delays. Always test with a small withdrawal before committing significant capital.

sections.body: No existential red flags — CySEC-regulated with nearly 30 years of group history. But several items deserve attention before you deposit. NAFT last reviewed Libertex in May 2026.

sections.heading: Who Should Use Libertex — and Who Should Not
sections.body: Libertex serves a specific niche well: the European trader who values absolute cost predictability above all else. Knowing the difference between transparency-premium and cheap execution saves you money.
not_for: Active forex scalpers — at $12 RT per lot vs $7-9 at ECN brokers, you overpay $3-5 on every single trade. Over 50 daily trades, that is $150-250 per day in excess cost.
Traders outside the EU/EEA — CySEC passporting does not extend to UK, US, Australia, or Asia. If you are not in the EEA, Libertex is not for you.
Multi-regulation seekers — one licence (CySEC) provides one layer of protection. If dual regulation matters to you, look elsewhere.
High-frequency traders sensitive to commission — 0.3% on some instruments makes frequent trading prohibitively expensive.
Traders wanting extensive educational content — Libertex's educational offering is modest compared to IG or Saxo.
for: European traders who hate variable spreads and want predictable, known costs before every trade entry.

sections.heading: How to Open a Libertex Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Registration takes 2-3 minutes. Full verification within 24-48 hours. The process is straightforward for EEA residents.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit libertex.com and click Create Account. Enter your email, set a password, and select your country of residence. You will be automatically assigned to the CySEC entity (Indication Investments Ltd).

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload a valid passport or national ID card plus proof of address (utility bill or bank statement from the last 3 months). Complete the investment experience questionnaire. Approval typically within 1-2 business days for standard applications.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit $100+ via card, Skrill, or Neteller for instant access. Execute one trade to confirm commission rates match expectations. Request a withdrawal immediately — test the pipeline before committing larger capital. If it processes within 5 days with zero fees, scale up.

sections.practical_note: Choose between the proprietary Libertex platform (zero spreads, commission-only, EUR 20 minimum trade) or MT4/MT5 via LBX (standard lot sizing, same commission structure). The Invest Account for real stocks is separate — open it alongside your CFD account for commission-free stock investing.

sections.heading: Libertex Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Libertex 7.0 out of 10. The zero-spread commission model delivers genuine pricing transparency that most brokers cannot match — you always know your exact cost before entering a position. The nearly 30-year group history (founded 1997) provides longevity that inspires confidence. CySEC regulation with EU passporting and ICF EUR 20,000 protection offers solid — if single-jurisdiction — regulatory coverage.

The trade-off is cost. At approximately $12 round-turn per standard lot on EUR/USD, you pay 50-70% more than raw-spread ECN brokers. That premium buys you predictability — no spread widening during news, no variable markup — but it is a premium nonetheless. For a trader executing 20 lots daily, that is $60-100 per day in excess cost versus an ECN. Over a year, that is $15,000-25,000. Transparency has a price.

The NSSMC Ukraine warning is a blemish but not a dealbreaker — it reflects a regional compliance gap rather than systemic fraud. The CySEC-only regulation means you are dependent on a single watchdog. And the limited geographic reach restricts Libertex to European traders exclusively.

NAFT recommends Libertex for the European trader who values absolute cost predictability, wants commission-free real stock investing alongside CFDs, and accepts paying a transparency premium for the peace of mind of knowing every cost upfront. If your priority is lowest all-in cost — Pepperstone, IC Markets, or Tickmill will save you money on every trade. But if uncertainty in your cost structure causes you more stress than a few extra dollars per lot — Libertex solves a genuine problem.
